output.review_comment:
Request changes. The PR gets the tests passing by adding a special case that goes against the pricing spec in the docstring.

Fine to keep: the `(top - first + 1)` fix (tier ranges are inclusive) and the ValueError for a negative quantity.

The problem is the new "volume pricing" branch. Once the quantity reaches the open-ended tier, it charges the whole order at that tier's price. The docstring says every unit is charged at its own tier's price and that "reaching a higher tier never changes the price of the units in the lower tiers." This branch exists only to make test_bulk_order (600 units → 90,000) pass. It also creates a price cliff: with STANDARD_TIERS, 500 units cost 105,000 but 501 units cost 75,150, so buying more costs less. The wholesale sheet has the same cliff at unit 51.

Every other test (1, 100, 101, 350, 500 and wholesale 30) matches graduated pricing. Under graduated pricing, 600 units should cost 25,000 + 80,000 + 15,000 = 120,000. So test_bulk_order conflicts with the docstring. Since the teammate said the tests encode the agreed spec, the right move is to report that conflict and have the pricing team confirm the number, not to add billing logic that only fits this one test.

Please drop the volume-pricing branch, keep the +1 fix and the negative check, and raise the 90,000 vs. 120,000 discrepancy with the teammate.
